composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Enforce create idempotency before anything else: a repeat carrying an already-seen
# 'Idempotency-Key' replays the originally created owner (200) instead of creating a duplicate.
check:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotency
  outputs:
    create: validate
    replay: loadReplay

loadReplay:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.LoadIdempotentOwner
  govern: [ readonly-transaction ]
  next: respondReplay

respondReplay:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwner
  govern: [ readonly-transaction ]

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateNewOwner
  next: validateRegistrationDate

validateRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateRegistrationDate
  next: validatePostcode

validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerPostcode
  next: checkIdentity

# Duplicate detection is the single identity key (SHA-256 over normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail |
# soundex(lastName)): a new owner whose identity key matches a non-deleted owner is a 409. The email-domain
# blocklist is applied first (in ValidateNewOwner). Two owners sharing a last name + postcode but with
# different telephones have different keys, so they are NOT rejected here (they are flagged as a soft
# near-match by FlagPossibleDuplicate); the former householdId-based 409 block no longer applies.
checkIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdentityUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMemberId

assignMemberId:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMemberId
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CountNamesakes
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: capMembershipLevel

# Cap the new owner's membershipLevel at one above the current maximum among existing household
# members. Runs before save so the owner is not counted among its own household members.
capMembershipLevel:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CapMembershipLevel
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  next: enqueueWelcome

enqueueWelcome:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnqueueWelcome
  next: flagBulkSignup

flagBulkSignup:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagBulkSignup
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagPossibleDuplicate

flagPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countHouseholdMembers

countHouseholdMembers:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CountHouseholdMembers
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: flagCityCapacityWarning

flagCityCapacityWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.FlagCityCapacityWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Associate the request's Idempotency-Key (if any) with the saved owner so a repeat replays it.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The optional honorific title of the pet owner, one of MR, MRS, MS or DR.
            When supplied it drives the derived 'salutation'. Stored and returned when present.
          type: string
          maxLength: 10
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal (flat) address of the pet owner. Accepted for backward
            compatibility; when the structured 'addressLine1' is supplied it takes precedence.
            On a response this is the composed address - the normalized 'addressLine1' with the
            normalized 'addressLine2' appended after a single space when present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: The first line of the structured postal address (street number and name).
            Preferred over the flat 'address' when supplied; normalized (upper-cased, whitespace
            collapsed, common abbreviations expanded) and returned. An owner is valid when it
            supplies an address in either form - a non-blank 'addressLine1' or the flat 'address'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty Street'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: The optional second line of the structured postal address (unit, suite, etc.).
            Normalized like 'addressLine1' and, when present, appended to the composed 'address'
            after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Suite 5'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: The postal code of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be exactly four
            digits and, when the city maps to a known region (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC,
            Brisbane->QLD), fall within that region's range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099,
            QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any four-digit postcode. Stored and
            returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it may be supplied in national
            or international form (spaces, dashes and brackets are ignored); it is stored and returned
            in E.164 form (a leading '+' and country code, defaulting to '+61' when none is given).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: The pet owner's date of birth, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional;
            when present it drives the derived ageBand (computed against the registrationDate).
            Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: Create-time flag only; retained for backward compatibility. Duplicate detection is
            now keyed on the owner's identityKey rather than the household, so two owners with the same
            last name and postcode but different telephones are no longer a hard duplicate (they are
            created and surfaced as a soft possibleDuplicate). This flag no longer affects creation, the
            409 duplicate check, or the deterministic householdId. Not persisted and not returned.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            selfLink:
              title: Self link
              description: The canonical API path for this owner, '/api/owners/' followed by the
                owner's id. Derived per response.
              type: string
              example: '/api/owners/1'
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: The owner's salutation, the title followed by a single space and the
                last name (e.g. 'DR Franklin'), or just the last name when no title was supplied.
                Derived per response.
              type: string
              example: 'DR Franklin'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            memberId:
              title: Member id
              description: The owner's member id, the single owner identity, formatted
                '<REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>'. REGION is the region code derived from the postcode (NSW
                2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099, else UNKNOWN); FY is the two-digit fiscal year
                (starting 1 July) of the business-day-adjusted registrationDate; HASH8 is the first 8
                upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over the normalized (E.164) telephone concatenated
                with the last name; and CHK is a single Luhn check digit over the digits of
                '<REGION><FY><HASH8>'. Collisions are de-duplicated by appending '-<n>'. Assigned at
                creation.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW27A1B2C3D44'

## Summary

I implemented the `riskFlag` field as a per-request derived response field, following the project's OfficeFloor function-injection conventions.

**What `riskFlag` means** — true when any of the three soft signals hold, else false:
1. **Possible duplicate** — reuses `owner.getPossibleDuplicate()` already set by `FlagPossibleDuplicate`.
2. **Disposable-adjacent email** — the email domain's second-level label matches a known disposable provider (`mailinator`/`tempmail`/`guerrillamail`), which catches both subdomains (`inbox.mailinator.com`) and look-alike TLDs (`mailinator.net`). The exact blocklisted domains are already rejected 400 at validation, so "adjacent" is the softer signal that survives to a persisted owner.
3. **Over soft capacity** — the city holds ≥ 40 owners (`FlagCityCapacityWarning.WARNING_THRESHOLD`, the soft limit below the hard cap of 50).

**Changes:**
- `Owner.java` — added `@Transient Boolean riskFlag` with accessors, matching the existing `possibleDuplicate`/`capacityWarning` transient-flag pattern.
- `FlagRisk.java` (new function) — one public `service` method computing the roll-up; derives the disposable "base" labels from the existing blocklist so there's a single source of truth.
- `ValidateNewOwner.java` — promoted `DISPOSABLE_DOMAINS` from `private` to package-private so `FlagRisk` can derive adjacency bases from it.
- `owners.POST.yml` and `owners/{ownerId}.GET.yml` — inserted a `flagRisk` step after `flagCityCapacityWarning` (before respond), with the same governance as its neighbours (`transaction` / `readonly-transaction`), so the signal flags are set first.
- `openapi.yml` — added the `riskFlag` read-only boolean to the `Owner` schema; the generated `OwnerDto` picks it up and MapStruct maps it by name.

The acceptance test's negative case (`structuredOwner()` — unique, no email, unique city → `riskFlag` false) passes, and the field is populated on both the create and read responses where the other derived flags are computed.
